title: Chicken Kiev
description: Golden crumbed chicken breast stuffed with garlic butter, served with a simple tomato cream sauce. A showstopper from the bistro era.

ingredients.notes: divided: 125g softened (for Chicken), 15g (for Tomato Cream Sauce)
Don't add too much all at once — you can't take it out once it's in.

method.instruction: Mix 125 g of softened unsalted butter with 4 crushed garlic cloves and 10 g chopped fresh parsley. Shape the mixture into a compact log, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and freeze until completely firm (at least 30 minutes).

Cut a deep pocket into the side of the chicken breast, being careful not to cut all the way through the meat. Insert the frozen garlic butter log into the pocket and seal the edges firmly by pressing the meat together.

Dust the stuffed breast lightly with plain flour, dip thoroughly in beaten egg, and coat with breadcrumbs. For extra security to prevent leaks, repeat the egg and breadcrumb steps to create a double crumb coating.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or deep pan to 180°C. Deep-fry the crumbed chicken for 8–10 minutes until deep golden brown and cooked through. The frozen butter will melt inside to baste the breast from within.
For the sauce: melt the remaining 15 g of unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced brown onion and cook until translucent, about 3–4 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Pour in 60 ml thickened cream and 15 ml tomato sauce. Stir and simmer for 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly to a light coating consistency. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Plate the cooked chicken breast and spoon the warm tomato cream sauce over it to serve immediately.

notes.title: Frozen Butter Log
notes.content: The garlic butter must be frozen solid before inserting. This prevents it from leaking out during crumbing and ensures it melts inside the chicken as it cooks, basting it from within.

notes.title: Double Crumb
notes.content: Double crumbing (flour, egg, breadcrumbs, egg, breadcrumbs again) gives a better seal and a thicker, crunchier crust that holds the butter in during frying.
